subject: Quantitative Ability
q: Find the median of 8, 9, 4, 7, 10.
explanation: In order: 4, 7, 8, 9, 10; the middle value is 8.

subject: Quantitative Ability
q: What is the median of the data 20, 10, 25, 22, 8, 12?

subject: Quantitative Ability
q: The heights of seven plants, in cm, are 28, 34, 42, 45, 25, 22, 31. What is the median height?
explanation: Arranged: 22, 25, 28, 31, 34, 42, 45; the 4th value, 31 cm, is the median.

subject: Quantitative Ability
q: Daily wages (Rs hundred) of eight workers: 12, 27, 15, 19, 24, 18, 14, 22. What is the median wage?

subject: Quantitative Ability
q: Goals scored by a team in eight matches: 0, 1, 2, 5, 5, 4, 3, 2. Find the median number of goals.

subject: Quantitative Ability
q: The six observations 13, 15, 17, x, 23, 25 are in increasing order and their median is 19. Find x.
explanation: With six values in order the median is (17 + x) ÷ 2 = 19, so x = 38 − 17 = 21.

subject: Quantitative Ability
q: If the value 27 is added to the data 3, 6, 7, 8, 11, what is the new median?
explanation: The six values in order are 3, 6, 7, 8, 11, 27; the median is the mean of the 3rd and 4th: 7.5.

subject: Quantitative Ability
q: What is the median of the first 11 odd natural numbers?
explanation: The first 11 odd numbers run from 1 to 21; the middle one (the 6th) is 11.

subject: Quantitative Ability
q: For the data 31, 25, 38, 30, 36, what is the difference between the mean and the median?
explanation: Mean = 160 ÷ 5 = 32; median = 31; difference = 1.

subject: Quantitative Ability
q: The numbers 21, 25, x, 41, 45 are in increasing order, and their median equals their mean. Find x.
explanation: The median is x and the mean is (132 + x) ÷ 5. Setting them equal: 5x = 132 + x, so x = 33.

subject: Quantitative Ability
q: Find the mode of 6, 6, 6, 5, 3, 9, 3.
explanation: 6 occurs three times, more often than any other value, so the mode is 6.

subject: Quantitative Ability
q: Shoe sizes sold in a day: 8, 7, 8, 8, 6, 8, 7, 6, 9. What is the modal size?
explanation: Size 8 appears 4 times, more than any other size.

subject: Quantitative Ability
q: The mode of the data 5, 2, 6, 6, 2, 8, x is 6. Which value must x take?
explanation: 6 and 2 each appear twice; only x = 6 makes 6 the single most frequent value.

subject: Quantitative Ability
q: Value: 1, 2, 3, 4; Frequency: 6, 2, 9, 3. What is the mode?
explanation: The value with the highest frequency (9) is 3, so the mode is 3.

subject: Quantitative Ability
q: The data 3, 3, 3, 4, 11, 9, 9 is changed by adding 9 to every value. What is the mode of the new data?
explanation: Adding 9 to every value shifts the mode by 9: 3 + 9 = 12.

subject: Quantitative Ability
q: The blood groups of twelve donors were A, A, B, A, AB, AB, B, A, B, AB, A, O. Which blood group is the mode?
explanation: Group A occurs 5 times, more than any other group.

subject: Quantitative Ability
q: What is the range of 18, 23, 52, 45, 58, 29?
explanation: Range = largest − smallest = 58 − 18 = 40.

subject: Quantitative Ability
q: If the minimum value in a set is 25 and its range is 15, what is the maximum value?
explanation: Range = max − min, so max = 25 + 15 = 40.

subject: Quantitative Ability
q: The range of a data set is 67 and its largest value is 70. What is its smallest value?
explanation: Smallest = largest − range = 70 − 67 = 3.

subject: Quantitative Ability
q: Minimum temperatures (°C) over a week were −4, −1, −4, 0, 8, 2, 9. What is the range?

subject: Quantitative Ability
q: A data set has a range of 32. If every value is multiplied by 3, what is the new range?
explanation: Multiplying every value by 3 multiplies the gap between the largest and smallest by 3: 3 × 32 = 96.

subject: Quantitative Ability
q: A data set has a range of 78. If 13 is added to every value, what is the new range?
explanation: Adding 13 to every value moves the largest and smallest by the same amount, so the range stays 78.

subject: Quantitative Ability
q: Sales (units): Mon 30, Tue 110, Wed 135, Thu 100, Fri 25. What percentage of the week's sales were made on Thursday?

subject: Quantitative Ability
q: Students by faculty: Arts 850, Science 300, Commerce 100, Engineering 750. What percentage of the students study Science?

subject: Quantitative Ability
q: A family's monthly spending (Rs): Food 500, Rent 6000, Education 1500, Other 7000. What percentage of the spending goes on rent?
explanation: Total spending = Rs 15,000; rent = Rs 6000; share = 40%.

subject: Quantitative Ability
q: Votes polled: Candidate A 100, Candidate B 600, Candidate C 1100, Candidate D 200. What percentage of the votes did Candidate B receive?
explanation: Total votes = 2000; B received 600, i.e. 30%.

subject: Quantitative Ability
q: A budget (Rs crore) is shown in a pie chart: Health 15, Defence 25, Education 40, Other 20. What is the central angle of the Education sector?
explanation: Education's share is 40 ÷ 100 = 40%; its sector angle is 40% of 360° = 144°.

subject: Quantitative Ability
q: Fruit sold (kg): Apples 280, Mangoes 80, Bananas 40. Mangoes make up what percentage of the fruit sold?
explanation: Total = 400 kg; mangoes = 80 kg; 80 ÷ 400 × 100 = 20%.

subject: Quantitative Ability
q: Production (tonnes): 2021 75, 2022 25, 2023 100, 2024 50. What percentage of the four-year total was produced in 2024?

subject: Quantitative Ability
q: Grades in a class: A 140, B 40, C 165, D 55. What percentage of the students got grade A or B?
explanation: Grades A and B: 140 + 40 = 180 of 400 students = 45%.

subject: Quantitative Ability
q: Favourite sport of respondents: Cricket 180, Hockey 45, Football 80, Squash 95. The number choosing cricket exceeds the number choosing football by what percentage of all respondents?
explanation: Cricket − football = 180 − 80 = 100; as a share of all 400 respondents that is 25%.

subject: Quantitative Ability
q: Monthly costs of a business (Rs thousand): Salaries 35, Rent 65, Transport 100, Utilities 200. What fraction of the total is spent on transport?
explanation: Transport 100 out of a total of 400: 100/400 = 1/4.

subject: Quantitative Ability
q: Sales of a shop (Rs lakh): 2021 250, 2022 400, 2023 399. What was the percentage increase in sales from 2021 to 2022?

subject: Quantitative Ability
q: The population of a town was 60,000 in 2015 and 78,000 in 2025. What was the percentage increase?

subject: Quantitative Ability
q: A country's exports (US$ billion): 2023 40, 2024 24. By what percentage did exports fall?

subject: Quantitative Ability
q: Enrolment at a school: 2019 80, 2020 116, 2021 132, 2022 140, 2023 164. In which year was the increase over the previous year the greatest?
explanation: Year-on-year increases: 2020: 36, 2021: 16, 2022: 8, 2023: 24; the greatest is in 2020.

subject: Quantitative Ability
q: Units sold: Shop X 120, Shop Y 156. What is the ratio of Shop X's sales to Shop Y's sales?
explanation: 120 : 156; dividing by 12 gives 10 : 13.

subject: Quantitative Ability
q: A student's marks in Mathematics: Term 1 40, Term 2 43, Term 3 44. By what percentage of the Term 1 mark did the mark rise by Term 3?
explanation: Rise from term 1 to term 3 = 44 − 40 = 4; 4 ÷ 40 × 100 = 10%.

subject: Quantitative Ability
q: Monthly profit (Rs thousand): Jan 200, Feb 210, Mar 147, Apr 162. In which month did profit fall compared with the previous month?
explanation: Only one month falls: March, from 210 to 147 (a 30% decrease); the others rise.

subject: Quantitative Ability
q: Wheat production (million tonnes): 2020 200, 2021 202, 2022 258, 2023 260. By what percentage was the 2023 production greater than the 2020 production?

subject: Quantitative Ability
q: The number of visitors to a park fell from 400 in March to 320 in April. What was the percentage decrease?

subject: Quantitative Ability
q: Students in a school — Boys: VI 21, VII 23, VIII 23, IX 27; Girls: VI 22, VII 21, VIII 24, IX 30. In which class is the ratio of girls to boys the highest?
explanation: Girls ÷ boys: VI 22/21, VII 21/23, VIII 24/23, IX 30/27; the largest ratio is in Class IX.

subject: Quantitative Ability
q: The mean of five numbers is 43. Four of them are 36, 46, 49 and 51. What is the fifth number?
explanation: Total needed = 5 × 43 = 215; known total = 182; fifth = 33.

subject: Quantitative Ability
q: A new number is added to the data 12, 12, 2, 2, 8, 6 so that the average does not change. What is the new number?
explanation: Adding a number equal to the mean leaves the mean unchanged: the mean is 42 ÷ 6 = 7.

subject: Quantitative Ability
q: A batsman's average over 4 innings is 50. How many runs must he score in the next innings to raise his average to 53?
explanation: He needs 5 × 53 = 265 runs in all; he has 4 × 50 = 200; so 65 are needed.

subject: Quantitative Ability
q: The mean of x, x + 4, x + 8, x + 12 and x + 16 is 44. What is x?
explanation: The mean of x, x + 4, …, x + 16 is the middle term x + 8 = 44, so x = 36.

subject: Quantitative Ability
q: Electricity bills: Jan Rs 800, Feb Rs 350, Mar ?, Apr Rs 900. The average bill for the four months is Rs 650. What was the March bill?
explanation: Four months at Rs 650 total Rs 2600; the other three months total Rs 2050; March = Rs 550.

subject: Quantitative Ability
q: The average age of five children born at intervals of 1 year is 24 years. What is the age of the youngest child?
explanation: Five ages at 1-year gaps are symmetric about the middle one, which equals the average 24; the youngest is 24 − 2 × 1 = 22.

subject: Quantitative Ability
q: A student scored 30, 27, 45 and 45 in four subjects. What must she score in the fifth subject to average 36?
explanation: She needs 5 × 36 = 180 marks in all; she has 147; so she needs 33.

subject: Quantitative Ability
q: The mean of 9 numbers is 16. When one number is removed, the mean of the rest is 12. What number was removed?
explanation: Total before = 9 × 16 = 144; after = 8 × 12 = 96; the excluded number is 48.

subject: Quantitative Ability
q: Three numbers are in the ratio 3 : 4 : 5 and their average is 40. What is the largest of them?
explanation: Sum = 3 × 40 = 120; 12 parts = 120, one part = 10; the largest is 5 × 10 = 50.

subject: Quantitative Ability
q: The mean of seven consecutive integers is 13. What is the largest of them?
explanation: Seven consecutive integers are centred on their mean 13, so they run from 10 to 16.

subject: Quantitative Ability
q: If a constant 8 is added to each observation of a data set whose mean is 34, the new mean is:
explanation: Adding 8 to every observation adds 8 to the mean: 34 + 8 = 42.

subject: Quantitative Ability
q: The mean of 9 observations is 15. A new observation 105 is added. What is the mean of the 10 observations?

subject: Quantitative Ability
q: The average of 9 numbers is 15. If each number is multiplied by 5, what is the new average?
explanation: Multiplying every number by 5 multiplies the average by 5: 5 × 15 = 75.

subject: Quantitative Ability
q: The mean of 15 observations was calculated as 41, but one value, 65, had been wrongly recorded as 20. What is the correct mean?
explanation: Correct total = 15 × 41 − 20 + 65 = 660; correct mean = 660 ÷ 15 = 44.

subject: Quantitative Ability
q: The average weight of 9 people rises by 1 kg when one of them, weighing 59 kg, is replaced by a new person. How much does the new person weigh?
explanation: The total rises by 9 × 1 = 9 kg, so the newcomer weighs 59 + 9 = 68 kg.

subject: Quantitative Ability
q: The average of 5 numbers is 55. If one number, 95, is removed, what is the average of the rest?
explanation: Total = 5 × 55 = 275; remove 95: 180; mean of 4 numbers = 45.

subject: Quantitative Ability
q: The average age of 32 students in a class is 11 years. When the teacher's age is included, the average rises by 1 year. How old is the teacher?
explanation: New total = 33 × 12 = 396; old total = 32 × 11 = 352; teacher = 44 years.

subject: Quantitative Ability
q: The mean of a set of prices is Rs 340. If every price is reduced by 40%, what is the new mean?
explanation: Reducing every value by 40% reduces the mean by 40%: 340 × 0.6 = 204.

subject: Quantitative Ability
q: The average of a set of numbers is 52. If 4 is subtracted from each number and the result is divided by 6, what is the new average?
explanation: Subtracting 4 makes the average 48; dividing by 6 makes it 8.

subject: Quantitative Ability
q: The average salary of 15 workers is Rs 17,000. When the manager's salary of Rs 33,000 is included, what is the new average?

subject: Quantitative Ability
q: The mean mark of 10 boys is 55 and that of 15 girls is 70. What is the mean mark of the whole class?

subject: Quantitative Ability
q: A library has an average of 740 visitors on Sundays and 470 on other days. What is the average number of visitors per day in a month of 30 days that begins with a Sunday?
explanation: A 30-day month starting on Sunday has 5 Sundays: (5 × 740 + 25 × 470) ÷ 30 = 515.

subject: Quantitative Ability
q: Section A has 40 students with an average score of 52; Section B has 20 students averaging 70. What is the combined average?

subject: Quantitative Ability
q: A shop sold 30 shirts at an average price of Rs 1140 and 20 shirts at an average of Rs 1280. What was the average price per shirt?

subject: Quantitative Ability
q: The average of 50 numbers is 70. The average of the first 40 of them is 55. What is the average of the remaining 10?
explanation: Total = 50 × 70 = 3500; first 40 total 2200; remaining 10 total 1300; average = 130.

subject: Quantitative Ability
q: In a factory, 15 workers earn an average of Rs 17,250 a month and 25 earn an average of Rs 20,250. What is the average monthly wage of all the workers?

subject: Quantitative Ability
q: In a group of 12 adults, the men average 66 kg and the women 54 kg, and the whole group averages 58 kg. How many men are in the group?

subject: Quantitative Ability
q: The average rainfall was 75 mm for the first 6 months of a period and 113 mm for the next 4 months. What was the average monthly rainfall over the ten months?

subject: Quantitative Ability
q: Find the mean of the distribution — Value: 1, 2, 3, 4, 5; Frequency: 8, 12, 3, 6, 11.

subject: Quantitative Ability
q: Marks (x): 10, 20, 30, 40; Number of students (f): 7, 6, 7, 5. What is the mean mark?
explanation: Σfx = 600, Σf = 25; mean = 24.

subject: Quantitative Ability
q: Children per family: 0, 1, 2, 3, 4; Number of families: 2, 6, 15, 6, 2. What is the mean number of children per family?
explanation: The frequencies are symmetric about 2 children, so Σfx ÷ Σf = 62 ÷ 31 = 2.

subject: Quantitative Ability
q: Value: 1, 2, 3, 4, 5; Frequency: 6, 6, 1, 7, 3. What is the median of this distribution?
explanation: There are 23 observations; the median is the 12th, which is 2 (cumulative frequencies 6, 12, 13, 20, 23).

subject: Quantitative Ability
q: Goals per match: 0, 1, 2, 3; Number of matches: 7, 9, 5, 11. How many goals were scored in all?
explanation: Total goals = Σ(goals × matches) = 0×7 + 1×9 + 2×5 + 3×11 = 52.

subject: Quantitative Ability
q: Daily wage (Rs): 500, 600, 700, 800; Number of workers: 11, 9, 1, 4. What is the mean daily wage?
explanation: Σfx = 14,800, Σf = 25; mean wage = Rs 592.

subject: Quantitative Ability
q: Shoe size: 6, 7, 8, 9; Pairs sold: 20, 15, 15, 10. What is the mean size sold?
explanation: Σfx = 435, Σf = 60; mean size = 7.25.

subject: Quantitative Ability
q: Score: 10, 20, 30, 40, 50; Number of candidates: 1, 8, 2, 9, 1. What is the median score?
explanation: With 21 observations, counting through the cumulative frequencies 1, 9, 11, 20, 21 shows the median is 30.

subject: Quantitative Ability
q: The mean of the distribution x: 1, 2, 3, 4; f: 5, k, 10, 3 is 2.5. Find k.
explanation: Σfx = 5 + 2k + 30 + 12 and Σf = 18 + k; setting Σfx = 2.5 × Σf gives k = 4.

subject: Quantitative Ability
q: Test score: 10, 20, 30, 40, 50; Students: 6, 1, 1, 4, 8. What percentage of the students scored more than 30?
explanation: Scores above 30 are 40 and 50: 4 + 8 = 12 of 20 students = 60%.

subject: Quantitative Ability
q: A box contains 7 red, 10 green and 6 blue toys. What is the probability that a toy picked at random is neither red nor green?
explanation: Neither red nor green means blue: 6 of the 23 toys, so 6/23.

subject: Quantitative Ability
q: A bag holds 3 red and 7 white balls. One ball is drawn at random. What is the probability that it is red?
explanation: 3 red out of 10 balls: P(red) = 3/10.

subject: Quantitative Ability
q: A jar has 4 red, 4 green and 10 blue marbles. If one marble is taken at random, what is the probability that it is not blue?
explanation: Not blue: 18 − 10 = 8 of 18 marbles, so 4/9.

subject: Quantitative Ability
q: A packet contains 3 mint, 6 orange and 3 lemon sweets. A sweet is taken without looking. What is the probability that it is lemon or orange?
explanation: Lemon or orange: 3 + 6 = 9 of 12 sweets, so 3/4.

subject: Quantitative Ability
q: The probability of rain tomorrow is 0.15. What is the probability that it will not rain?

subject: Quantitative Ability
q: Which of the following describes all the values a probability can take?
explanation: A probability is 0 for an impossible event, 1 for a certain event, and never outside this range.

subject: Quantitative Ability
q: A bag contains 20 marbles, each red or blue. The probability of drawing a red marble is 2/5. How many blue marbles are there?

subject: Quantitative Ability
q: A bag has 3 red and 9 blue balls. How many green balls must be added so that the probability of drawing a green ball becomes 1/4?

subject: Quantitative Ability
q: The probability of drawing a white ball from a bag is 5/8. If the bag contains 45 white balls, how many balls are there altogether?
explanation: 45 is 5/8 of the total, so the total is 45 × 8 ÷ 5 = 72.

subject: Quantitative Ability
q: A letter is chosen at random from the word ISLAMABAD. What is the probability that it is the letter A?
explanation: ISLAMABAD has 9 letters, of which 3 are A: probability 3/9 = 1/3.

subject: Quantitative Ability
q: A month of the year is chosen at random. What is the probability that it has 31 days?
explanation: Seven months (January, March, May, July, August, October, December) have 31 days: 7/12.

subject: Quantitative Ability
q: A class of 18 students has 8 girls. If one student is chosen at random, what is the probability that the student is a boy?

subject: Quantitative Ability
q: A fair die is thrown once. What is the probability of getting a prime number?
explanation: The primes on a die are 2, 3 and 5: 3/6 = 1/2 (1 is not prime).

subject: Quantitative Ability
q: A fair six-sided die is rolled. What is the probability that the number shown is greater than 4?
explanation: Numbers greater than 4: 5, 6 — 1/3.

subject: Quantitative Ability
q: When an ordinary die is rolled, what is the probability of getting a multiple of 3?
explanation: Multiples of 3 on a die are 3 and 6: 2/6 = 1/3.

subject: Quantitative Ability
q: A die is rolled once. What is the probability that the number is odd or greater than 3?
explanation: Odd numbers or numbers above 3: 1, 3, 4, 5, 6 — 5/6.

subject: Quantitative Ability
q: A fair die is tossed. What is the probability that the number obtained is a factor of 6?
explanation: The factors of 6 are 1, 2, 3 and 6: 4/6 = 2/3.

subject: Quantitative Ability
q: A fair die is rolled. What is the probability of not getting a 4?
explanation: Only one of the six equally likely faces shows 4; so P(not 4) = 1 − 1/6 = 5/6.

subject: Quantitative Ability
q: A die numbered 1 to 6 is rolled. What is the probability of a number that is both even and greater than 4?
explanation: Even and greater than 4: 6 — 1/6.

subject: Quantitative Ability
q: An ordinary die is thrown. What is the probability that it shows a perfect square?
explanation: The perfect squares on a die are 1 and 4: 2/6 = 1/3.
